title: Hydraulic Turbine
model_title: Francis Hydraulic Turbine (Vertical Shaft) with Generator

introduction.definition: A Francis turbine is a reaction water turbine. Water from the penstock fills the spiral casing, passes the stay vanes and adjustable wicket gates and flows inward through the runner, turning it, then leaves down the draft tube. The gates control flow; the vertical shaft drives a generator.
key_points: Reaction turbine — full of water, pressure drops across the runner
Wicket gates control flow and power
introduction.summary: A Francis hydraulic turbine converts the pressure and velocity of water into shaft power. Water from the penstock fills the spiral casing, passes the stay vanes and the adjustable wicket gates — which set the flow and give it swirl — and flows inward through the runner, turning it. The water leaves downward through the draft tube, which recovers energy. The vertical shaft drives a generator above.

foundation: Embedded in reinforced concrete; spiral casing and draft tube liner concreted in place.
alignment: Shaft line plumb and centred to tight limits; guide bearing clearances set.
piping: Support suction and discharge piping independently so no pipe strain reaches the casing; fit flexible connections where vibration or thermal movement is expected.
Install inlet filters/strainers and isolation valves; add drains and vents.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

routine.task: Monitor vibration, bearing temperatures, gate position and head-cover pressure.

periodic.task: Check wicket gate shear pins and bushings.

overhaul.task: Repair cavitation damage on runner; inspect draft tube.

lubrication: Oil-lubricated guide and thrust bearings; greased gate bushings (or self-lubricated).

remedies: Weld repair with stainless; operate in good zone

video_tutorials.title: Hydraulic Turbine — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Hydraulic Turbine.
A Francis turbine is a reaction water turbine.
Water from the penstock fills the spiral casing, passes the stay vanes and adjustable wicket gates and flows inward through the runner, turning it, then leaves down the draft tube.
The gates control flow; the vertical shaft drives a generator.
Typical applications include hydropower plants (medium heads ~ 40–600 m); pumped storage (reversible pump-turbines); small hydro.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Spiral Casing (Scroll) & Inlet Pipe, Francis Runner (crown, band, 13 blades), Shaft & Generator Rotor, Draft Tube (cone, elbow & diffuser).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Hydraulic Turbine works.
Water enters the spiral casing from the penstock.
Stay vanes and wicket gates guide the water and set the flow.
Water flows inward through the runner blades, turning the runner.
The water leaves downward through the draft tube, which recovers kinetic energy.
The shaft turns the generator above.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Hydraulic Turbine — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Hydraulic Turbine.
Monitor vibration, bearing temperatures, gate position and head-cover pressure.
Check wicket gate shear pins and bushings.
Repair cavitation damage on runner; inspect draft tube.
Watch for cavitation erosion: pitting on blades, noise. Common cause: low tailwater/setting, off-design operation.
Watch for draft-tube pressure pulsation: vibration at part load. Common cause: vortex rope.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
